acceptance.given: Aggregate evaluation receives matrix evidence whose target identity differs from the aggregate target.

oracle.expected: Aggregate status is invalid and publication/acceptance is refused after wrong-target evidence is detected.
forbidden: Aggregate remains valid or is accepted despite wrong-target matrix evidence.
oracle.observable: Runtime aggregate verdict and acceptance gate record target-mismatch invalidation.

acceptance.then: The aggregate is marked invalid and cannot be accepted.
acceptance.when: The matrix-evidence target identity is checked during aggregate evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute aggregate evaluation with matrix evidence bound to a different target and assert the aggregate invalidation and acceptance gate rejects it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Detect target identity mismatch in matrix evidence and invalidate the aggregate before acceptance.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; reverting restores prior aggregate evaluation behavior.

slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Aggregate verdict is invalid and no acceptance or publication authorization is emitted when evidence target differs.

acceptance.given: Exact Cover validation is run against the complete set of atomic obligations and their mapped witnesses.

oracle.expected: Validation reports bidirectional Exact Cover for every atomic obligation with zero orphan obligations or one-way mappings.
forbidden: Any atomic obligation lacks a bidirectional Exact Cover relationship.
Exact Cover exists in only one direction.
oracle.observable: Validator output contains complete two-way obligation-to-witness coverage and zero-orphan result.

acceptance.then: All atomic obligations have bidirectional Exact Cover.
acceptance.when: The Exact Cover validator evaluates obligation, assertion, selector, command, runtime-evidence, and witness mappings.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run Exact Cover validation against a fixture with an omitted reverse mapping or orphan atomic obligation and require a nonzero validation result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate bidirectional Exact Cover completeness and reject orphan or one-way atomic-obligation mappings.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No runtime schema change; rollback restores previous validation rules.

slice_hint.state_transition: coverage unvalidated -> validating -> complete bidirectional cover or rejected with orphan or one-way diagnostic
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validator emits success only when every atomic obligation has both forward and reverse Exact Cover relationships and zero orphans.

acceptance.given: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages participate in one evaluation or rollback workflow.

oracle.expected: Inspection and execution checks show independently owned mutable state and evidence for each component, and mutating one component cannot alter another component's execution or result.
forbidden: Any listed component shares mutable state with another listed component.
Cross-component mutable-state sharing permits one component to alter another component's execution or result.
oracle.observable: Isolation test artifacts identify distinct state roots and owners and demonstrate mutation containment across all listed components.

acceptance.then: Each listed component operates with independently controlled mutable state, preventing cross-component state contamination.
acceptance.when: The isolation check inspects state and evidence ownership and runs controlled cross-component mutation probes.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the isolation probe with a shared mutable state or evidence location and require the boundary check to fail with the owning components identified.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Give every evaluation and rollback component an independent mutable-state and evidence boundary and reject cross-component contamination.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: State layout remains backward-compatible; rollback removes isolation changes without migrating persisted data.

slice_hint.state_transition: shared or unspecified state -> component-scoped state -> isolation verified
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Isolation evidence shows five distinct mutable-state boundaries and mutation of one boundary leaves all other component results unchanged.

acceptance.given: An external process is launched under configured time and output budgets.

oracle.expected: The execution records a deterministic terminal state, such as success, failure, or budget exhaustion, within the bounded budget.
forbidden: The external process ends in an indeterminate or nondeterministic terminal state.
oracle.observable: Process execution record contains terminal classification, exit or timeout reason, and bounded completion evidence.

acceptance.then: The external process is in a deterministic terminal state.
acceptance.when: The process executor observes process completion, timeout, or output-budget exhaustion and classifies the terminal outcome.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute an external process that exceeds or ambiguously reaches its budget and require deterministic timeout or budget-exhausted classification rather than an indeterminate result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bound external execution time and output and classify every completion, failure, timeout, or budget exhaustion into a deterministic terminal state.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Execution record schema remains compatible; rollback restores prior process classification behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: running -> completed, failed, timed-out, or budget-exhausted -> deterministic terminal verdict
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every launched process yields one stable terminal classification before the configured time or output budget is exceeded.
